Complete Empirical Research Plan  

================================================================  
1. Identification Strategy  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Method: Two–way-fixed-effects Difference-in-Differences (DID) complemented with an event-study dynamic specification.  

Why appropriate  
• We observe the same firms several years before and after a discrete policy change that expanded credit to a well-defined group (SMEs).  
• No obvious running variable with a single cutoff that regulators strictly enforced (rules are based on size but compliance is imperfect), so a clean RDD is less convincing.  
• The policy was not rolled out differentially across regions or industries, so staggered adoption is not an issue—one national “shock” → classical DID.  
• Firm-level panel allows us to net out time-invariant firm heterogeneity (firm FE) and macro shocks common to all firms (year FE).  
• Event-study coefficients visualize pre-trends and the dynamic path of treatment effects.  

================================================================  
2. Treatment and Control Definition  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Treatment variable  
Treated = 1 if a firm satisfied the official SME eligibility criterion in the first year before the program (t₀ – 1) and therefore became eligible for subsidized/priority credit when the program starts.  
  • Regulation defines SME as (for example) “≤ 250 employees OR ≤ INR 500 mn in assets.”  
  • We code treatment using pre-policy size to avoid endogenous status switching.  

Control group  
Firms that were just above the SME cutoff in t₀ – 1 (e.g., 251–400 employees or INR 500–800 mn assets). They resemble treated firms ex-ante but were ineligible.  

Treatment timing  
Policy announcement year = 2008 (t = 0). We define Post = 1 for 2008 + .  

Optional robustness: broaden control to all ineligible firms, run entropy balancing / propensity-score re-weighting.  

================================================================  
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
A1 Parallel trends: In the absence of the program, outcome trends (credit received, investment, sales, profits) for eligible and near-eligible firms would have evolved similarly.  
 • Plausibility: Both groups are contiguous in size and operate in same markets; no concurrent SME-specific shock is known.  
 • Test: Graph and regress pre-policy leads in an event-study; coefficients should be ≈ 0.  

A2 No differential shocks: No other policy simultaneously targeted only SMEs. Check policy timeline.  

A3 Stable composition: Firms do not deliberately resize just before the reform (we use pre-policy size), and attrition is unrelated to treatment.  
 • Plausibility: Resizing within one year is costly; we will show balance in exits.  

A4 SUTVA / no spillovers: Credit diverted to treated SMEs does not systematically crowd out credit for marginally larger firms.  
 • We discuss banking-sector capacity; include bank-year FE robustness.  

================================================================  
4. Main Threats and Mitigation  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
1. Endogenous classification (manipulation around threshold)  
  • McCrary density test on pre-policy size.  
  • Placebo DID using alternative cutoffs; results should disappear.  

2. Differential pre-trends  
  • Estimate event-study; drop sectors where pre-trends differ; interact with sector-specific time trends as robustness.  

3. Spillovers / credit reallocation  
  • Bank-level exposure IV (e.g., pre-policy share of SME lending at the firm’s main bank) to isolate exogenous credit supply.  
  • Include bank-year fixed effects to soak up supply shocks common to all clients of a bank.  

================================================================  
5. R Code Outline (executable)  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
```r
# 0. Packages ---------------------------------------------------
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)        # fast fixed-effects
library(broom)
# --------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Data -------------------------------------------------------
df <- read_csv("india_sme_credit.csv")

# 2. Variable construction -------------------------------------
policy_year <- 2008

df <- df %>%
  mutate(post        = as.integer(year >= policy_year),
         eligible_pre= if_else(year == policy_year - 1 &
                               (employees <= 250 | assets <= 500e6), 1L, 0L)) %>%
  group_by(firm_id) %>%
  mutate(treated = max(eligible_pre, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%  # fixed treatment status
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(did = treated * post,
         ln_invest = log1p(investment),
         ln_sales  = log1p(sales),
         ln_credit = log1p(credit_received))

# keep firms with size in bandwidth for cleaner control group
df <- df %>% filter(employees <= 400 | assets <= 800e6)

# 3. DID main spec ---------------------------------------------
spec_main <- feols(ln_credit ~ treated*post | firm_id + year, 
                   cluster = "firm_id", data = df)
summary(spec_main)

# 4. Event-study -----------------------------------------------
df <- df %>%
  mutate(event_time = year - policy_year) 

spec_event <- feols(ln_credit ~ i(event_time, treated, ref = -1) | 
                      firm_id + year, cluster = "firm_id", data = df)
iplot(spec_event, ref.line = 0)

# 5. Robustness: placebo reform in 2005 -------------------------
df_placebo <- df %>% mutate(post_placebo = as.integer(year >= 2005),
                             did_placebo = treated * post_placebo)

spec_placebo <- feols(ln_credit ~ did_placebo | firm_id + year, 
                      cluster = "firm_id", data = df_placebo %>% filter(year <= 2007))
summary(spec_placebo)
```

================================================================  
6. Expected Results  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Theory predicts relaxing credit constraints raises borrowing and capital formation; diminishing returns temper the effect on profits.  
Priors (treated relative to control, average 3-5 years post):  
• Credit received: +25 – 35 %.  
• Fixed investment: +15 – 25 %.  
• Sales: +10 %.  
• Profits: +5 %.  

================================================================  
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
C1 Parallel trends holds (pre-trend evidence)……………… 1  
C2 No simultaneous SME-specific policies…………………… 0.8  
C3 Stable treatment definition / no sorting………………… 0.7  
C4 No spillovers / interference…………………………………… 0.6  
C5 Correct standard-error clustering…………………………… 1  
Average ≈ 0.82 → design is reasonably credible but not bullet-proof.
